description: The one numbering of the network ports of an A.R.M.O.R. installation. The CM5 installer, the Docker stack, the firewall script, the server, Studio and the apps read their ports from here (the generated files are written by tools/generate_ports.py).

server.note: ARMOR-SERVER: the API and the ingest

studio.note: ARMOR-STUDIO: the web console (its proxy reaches the server)

mqtt.note: the plain listener of the broker (never the standard 1883, which other software may use)

voice.note: ARMOR-VOICE-AI: the gateway of the wall panel

mqtt_tls.note: the optional encrypted door of the broker

https.note: the optional TLS proxy of the Docker stack in front of Studio

acme_http.note: the plain port of the TLS proxy, for the check of a public certificate

scan.description: tests/test_ports.py looks for the old numbers (the ones in 'legacy') in the files of the repositories that exist next to this one, except the entries of 'allowed'.

allowed.why: 8080 is a port IP cameras answer on, not one of ours
